📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that despite the contemporary art world’s increased attention to women’s experiences and the politics of care in its public-facing programming, working mothers employed by London’s galleries and auction houses face widespread discrimination, according to a newly introduced study. As reported by the Art Newspaper today, a survey of 50 employees working in the UK capital’s commercial art sector has found that, for many, having children comes at considerable professional cost.

The study, conducted by Kate McMillan and Cleo Roberts-Komireddi and published today in the European Journal of Cultural Studies, looked at the extent to which pregnancy and maternity affected career progression among art world workers. Moving beyond previous studies centered on fine artists or senior directors, it focused on lower-paid, non-artist roles such as sales, administration, and marketing. Related Articles Recent Key Departures at Phillips Point to a Pivot in Strategy The Year in Gallery Closures: A Collapse or a Transition to a Smarter Market?

In a recent development, roberts-Komireddi and McMillan’s research, which also included 12 in-depth interviews, reveals an industry “marred by implicit and explicit expectations that often result in workers needing to choose between their careers and being parents,” they write. Three quarters of respondents felt that motherhood had impeded career advancement, while 20 percent mentioned they had been explicitly denied promotion.

The authors found poor and sometimes illegal practices across the industry, including employees being “managed” out of their roles while on maternity leave. Such practices, they note, are made possible by a lack of formal human resource structures—only half of the respondence worked for organizations with dedicated HR staff, and just 60 percent noted their workplace had a specific parental leave policy. They additionally blamed the art market’s pervasive culture of secrecy.

Class and wealth also play a role in shaping employee experience, the study suggests. For junior employees on modest salaries, the cost of childcare can make travel and attendance at evening events difficult and increase the likelihood of discrimination on the job. At the same time, a lack of resources makes challenging such discrimination daunting, with many women instead choosing to take a less senior position, move into freelance work, or leave the art world.

Roberts-Komireddi and McMillan’s study spanned small galleries to multinational auction houses and found problems across the board. As they say in their report, “A lack of accountability pervades the sector.”.

Say What? 7 Tips to Unclog Your Blocked Ears

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1277 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Greatist

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure might be behind your clogged ears.
  • In a recent development, whether it’s from a cold, allergies, or changes in air pressure, blocked ears can disrupt your day-to-day activities and even cause discomfort.
  • Clogging can happen either on the inside or the outside of your eardrum.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Earwax buildup, allergies, infections, or changes in air pressure might be behind your clogged ears. There are many easy ways to get relief at home. Whether it’s from a cold, allergies, or changes in air pressure, blocked ears can disrupt your day-to-day activities and even cause discomfort. Thankfully, there are several effective methods to help unclog your ears and restore your hearing. Listen up! Why are my ears clogged? Clogging can happen either on the inside or the outside of your eardrum. Here are the most common ways your ears can get blocked: Earwax in the outer ear helps prevent particles and excess water from entering the middle ear. However, if earwax builds up too much outside the eardrum, it can cause a blockage. If you’ve been swimming recently, some water might be stuck in your ear canal, pushing against your eardrum. When that water hangs around too long, it can lead to a swimmer’s ear, an outer ear infection. Sinus infections, ear infections, and Eustachian tube dysfunction can pressure your eardrum’s inner side. Allergies can cause uncomfortable inflammation and congestion in your ears. Your sinuses, throat, and ears are connected, so when you feel stuffed up and sniffly, your inner ear feels the pain too. Changes in air pressure, like when you fly, can cause uncomfortable ear pressure. Best clogged ear remedies 1. Pop and unclog The easiest way to unclog your ears is by “popping” them. Just pinch your nose shut, seal your lips, and gently blow. This simple technique, known as the Valsalva maneuver, won’t clear earwax or fluid but is a common trick people use on planes. 2. Swallow, yawn, or chew The Eustachian tubes connect your middle ear to the back of your throat. They briefly open when you swallow, yawn, or chew. Altitude changes can cause these tubes to close, but chewing gum or yawning can help reopen them. Alternatively, you can try the Toynbee maneuver, where you hold your nose and swallow. 3. Ear drops Over-the-counter (OTC) ear drops can soften and dissolve excess earwax. If you prefer a DIY approach, warm a small amount of mineral oil and use an eye dropper to apply a few drops into your ear for a few minutes. Pro tip: Baby oil or olive oil can also be used, but make sure it’s not too hot. Additionally, diluted hydrogen peroxide drops can be helpful. 4. Warmth and gravity To loosen up clogged earwax, use a warm, damp washcloth as a compress. Lie down with the clogged ear facing down against the heated washcloth. Gravity and heat will help the earwax move along more easily. 5. Hit the steam room Steam can help drain sinuses and alleviate pressure in your inner ear. Close the bathroom door, let the hot shower run for a while, and then luxuriate with deep, cleansing breaths. 6. Take allergy medication Because your throat, sinuses, and ears are interconnected, any sickness affecting your sinuses or throat can also impact your ears. Over-the-counter antihistamines, decongestants, or nasal sprays can relieve sniffles, coughs, and ear discomfort. 7. Rinse away the gunk Rinsing your nasal passages with a medication-free saline solution can help reduce congestion and clear out mucus that might be causing ear blockage. You can also consider investing in a nasal irrigation system for more thorough mucus clearing. When to see your doctor Have you been unable to unclog your ears for a few days, or are you experiencing severe pain, fever, dizziness, hearing loss, fluid discharge, or unusual odor? If so, it’s crucial to contact your healthcare provider promptly. These symptoms may indicate an infection that needs medical attention. What not to do when you have clogged ears Cotton swabs: Q-tips and other cotton swabs to remove earwax can push it further into your ear canal, so don’t do it. Candling: Ear candles might seem like a fun party trick, but there’s no science to prove they work, and they’ve been shown to cause injuries. Sprays: Decongestant nasal sprays can be helpful, but using them too long can lead to rebound congestion. In a recent development, whether it’s from a cold, allergies, or changes in air pressure, blocked ears can disrupt your day-to-day activities and even cause discomfort. Thankfully, there are several effective methods to help unclog your ears and restore your hearing. Listen up!

Recent findings suggest that the easiest way to unclog your ears is by “popping” them. Just pinch your nose shut, seal your lips, and gently blow. This simple technique, known as the Valsalva maneuver, won’t clear earwax or fluid but is a common trick people use on planes.

The Eustachian tubes connect your middle ear to the back of your throat. They briefly open when you swallow, yawn, or chew. Altitude changes can cause these tubes to close, but chewing gum or yawning can help reopen them. Alternatively, you can try the Toynbee maneuver, where you hold your nose and swallow.

Over-the-counter (OTC) ear drops can soften and dissolve excess earwax. If you prefer a DIY approach, warm a small amount of mineral oil and use an eye dropper to apply a few drops into your ear for a few minutes.

Industry observers note that to loosen up clogged earwax, use a warm, damp washcloth as a compress. Lie down with the clogged ear facing down against the heated washcloth. Gravity and heat will help the earwax move along more easily.

In a recent development, steam can help drain sinuses and alleviate pressure in your inner ear. Close the bathroom door, let the hot shower run for a while, and then luxuriate with deep, cleansing breaths.

Because your throat, sinuses, and ears are interconnected, any sickness affecting your sinuses or throat can also impact your ears.

Over-the-counter antihistamines, decongestants, or nasal sprays can relieve sniffles, coughs, and ear discomfort.

Rinsing your nasal passages with a medication-free saline solution can help reduce congestion and clear out mucus that might be causing ear blockage. You can also consider investing in a nasal irrigation system for more thorough mucus clearing.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Industry observers note that “I see it personally as a revolution, not an evolution,” McCartney told Dezeen from the LeBron James Innovation Center in Oregon.
  • Recent findings suggest that tuned Air was designed to give Nike much greater control of how air is used within the midsole to provide cushioning and support.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Photography courtesy of Nike.

It has been revealed that sportswear brand Nike has unveiled the 3D-printed air bags that will be used for its next generation of air-filled trainers. In this interview, the brand’s chief innovation, design & product officer Phil McCartney explains why it is a technological and performance advance.

Industry observers note that “I see it personally as a revolution, not an evolution,” McCartney told Dezeen from the LeBron James Innovation Center in Oregon. “It’s a huge stride forward.”.

Recent findings suggest that tuned Air was designed to give Nike much greater control of how air is used within the midsole to provide cushioning and support. Using a combination of proprietary 3D printing and “selective lamination” allows Nike to create midsoles that perform in different ways under different parts of the foot.

Informed by the raised vibrant colours on magazine covers, the airbag is built up from layers of ink.

“We can engineer the structure and tune the structure in the heel differently to the forefoot,” said McCartney.

“We can also tune the height, so you can have a variety of different heights, and we can tune the structure inside.”.

Nike unveiled the technology and concept images for a running shoe today, and is planning for the first Nike Tuned Air trainer to be launched next year.

The trainers will be the first in what Nike sees as a third major generation of its air-filled shoes, since Nike CEO Phil Knight worked with inventor Frank Rudy to use a cushioning system filled with gas in the late 1970s.

Following the Nike Air Tailwind in 1978, Nike developed Air Max in the 1980s and Air Zoom in the 1990s.

According to recent reports, “At its core, Air, for 50 years, has been this magical combination of lightweight, cushioned and resilient – it doesn’t break down over time,” remarked McCartney. “That’s why from day one when Phil [Knight] struck the deal with Frank Rudy, we’ve been so committed to it – it just delivers a really unique benefit.”.

“If Max Air is about maximal cushioning and impact protection, Zoom Air is more about responsiveness and snappiness,” he continued. “Tuned Air, because of this proprietary ink and selective lamination process, allows us to literally tune the sensation within the airbag, which enables us to sort of move free from the constraints of typical geometry and shape.”.

According to McCartney, this change in how the airbags are manufactured opens up possibilities, especially in customisation.

“It is the first step in exploring all the different places that this will go,” noted McCartney. “The capability and what we’re able to do with this proprietary ink and the selective lamination allows us to really unlock the real potential of air.”.

“It also creates this canvas for all the design explorations that we’ve always wanted to do, but the limitations of the manufacturing process didn’t allow,” he continued.

“So now the handcuffs are off in terms of it being a canvas – what expressions do we want to explore? What different visuals, geometries, and different ways to articulate the benefit can we explore? We’re looking at all of that. “.

Industry observers note that while the air-filled midsole has been manufactured, the trainer is still in development. However, McCartney expects the shoe to look close to the concept render that was revealed today.

“There’ll be a few modifications,” he stated. “Knowing where the design is going to go. It’s pretty representative as an illustration, but it isn’t the final design.” He noted that the final air bag design will be close to the prototype.

“What we’re exploring now is how do we take the idea of lightweight cushioning and this idea of tuned [and find] what that looks like in an expression and an experience on the upper.”.

One key design element that will feature in the commercial release next year will be the full-length, visible air bag, which McCartney noted is an “important part of the design and important part of this platform”.

Sources indicate that the midsoles are the latest innovation in Nike’s exploration of using air within footwear and apparel. While it has made millions of shoes containing air, it has also recently unveiled the inflating Air Milano Jacket at 2026 Winter Olympics and its Radical AirFlow t-shirts that counterintuitively use more material to make a wearer cooler.

In all the areas of innovation that McCartney oversees at Nike, air is where he sees the most potential.

“There’s a number of areas, but if I had to pick one, I think that [air] is the platform that intrigues us most, that drives our creativity the most, that also translates into the biggest athlete benefit. And I mean athlete in the broadest sense of the term – if you’ve got a body, you’re an athlete.”.

Sources indicate that “We’re really intrigued and fascinated by the notion of being able to harness what’s all around us to further performance,” remarked McCartney. “That started in footwear, obviously. This is the next revolution.”.

Photography courtesy of Nike.

Tangerines are not just tasty — they’re a powerhouse of nutrients. Packed with tangy flavor and vibrant orange color, these citrus delights offer a host of health benefits. From boosting your immune system to rejuvenating your skin, tangerines are nutrient-rich allies for your well-being. Let’s delve into their nutritional profile and discover why they’re a smart addition to your diet.

Tangerines are nutritional powerhouses. Here’s what each of these little champs pack under their orange belts:.

Tangerines are teeny cousins of the orange but with a thinner, easier-to-peel skin. They boast a sweet and juicy flavor and pack a ton of vitamins, particularly vitamin C, as well as minerals like potassium, antioxidants, and dietary fiber.

Industry observers note that these tiny bursts of sunshine have many benefits that can significantly enhance your health. Here’s why you might want to make tangerines a regular part of your diet:.

Sources indicate that tangerines are loaded with vitamin C, turning them into tiny, tasty guardians for your health. This crucial vitamin supercharges your immune system by enhancing the function and effectiveness of white blood cells, which are essential for fighting off pathogens and infections. By improving the activity and response of these cells, vitamin C helps your body combat a wide range of infections more effectively.

Therefore, regular consumption of these mini-oranges satisfies your taste buds and boosts your body’s defense mechanisms — a win-win!

Want that glow? Tangerines have got you covered. They’re high in potassium, a real game-changer for regulating hydration and balancing fluid levels in your skin cells. This essential mineral keeps your skin cells plump and hydrated, warding off pesky, dry, dull patches.

Plus, potassium supports the removal of toxins and wastes, which means clearer, more radiant skin.

Tangerines are also a fantastic source of vitamin A, which strengthens the outer layer of your skin, smoothing out wrinkles and reducing fine lines. Along with vitamin C, it’s a potent antioxidant, protecting your skin from the damaging and aging effects of free radicals.

Are you having tummy troubles? Tangerines can help with a fiber boost that keeps things moving smoothly along your digestive tract.

These zesty little superheroes are your gut’s upcoming best friends. They’re loaded with fiber that bulks up and softens things down there, making your bathroom visits smooth and speedy. This fruity fix helps manage everything from irregular pit stops to those bloated bleurgh days.

Fiber also balances your gut flora, promoting a healthy microbial environment in your intestines. This balance is crucial for optimal digestion, nutrient absorption, and immune function.

So, grab a tangerine to remedy your belly blues next time your gut feels out of whack.

In a recent development, tangerines are a dynamo when it comes to battling serious health baddies like cancer and heart disease. These little orange wonders are loaded with flavonoids, natural compounds that help with heart health and cancer prevention.

According to recent reports, flavonoids help relax the blood vessels, lowering blood pressure levels and reducing the strain on your heart. This helps keep your ticker ticking smoothly and reduces the risk of cardiovascular diseases like heart attacks and strokes.

It has been revealed that but wait, there’s more! When it comes to cancer, flavonoids mess with the bad guys — cancer cells — stopping them from multiplying and spreading their nonsense around your body.

Industry observers note that keep your peepers sharp with a dose of vitamin A from tangerines. This essential nutrient and compounds like beta-carotene shield your eyes from age-related issues and support healthy vision. It plays a key role in creating rhodopsin, a protein in your eyes that allows you to see in low-light conditions.

Munching on tangerines helps keep your night vision in superhero shape and supports overall eye function, keeping your peepers sharp and responsive.

Furthermore, tangerines contain other essential eye health nutrients, like lutein and zeaxanthin. These antioxidants are found in high concentrations in the retina, where they help filter blue light and prevent oxidative damage, further protecting the eyes from conditions like cataracts.

Sure, tangerines are delish and make your taste buds do a happy dance, but they’re also packed with nutrients that can seriously amp up your well-being.

Recent findings suggest that from giving your immune system a high-five to keeping your heart beating like a healthy drum, tangerines are basically wellness wrapped in a bright orange peel. So, go grab one and make it your main squeeze!

  • In a decision dated October 26 and filed on November 16, New York Supreme Court Justice James G.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A Upcoming York judge has refused to throw out a lawsuit over a 15th-century Fra Angelico painting that the heirs to the Bic pen fortune say was stolen by their family chauffeur and later sold by the late art dealer Richard Feigen.

In a decision dated October 26 and filed on November 16, New York Supreme Court Justice James G. Clynes rejected an attempt by Feigen’s estate and associated businesses to get the case dismissed. Their main argument? The family had waited too long to sue.

Industry observers note that “No family should lose a treasured work of art simply because the people who handled this stolen property were sophisticated dealmakers,” Luke Nikas, a lawyer for the Bich family, told ARTnews. The Bich family is determined to recover what belongs to them, and today’s decision is an important step toward achieving that result.” The ruling is good news for the Bich heirs, though there’s still a long way to go. The judge hasn’t decided who owns the painting, or even whether it was stolen. Related Articles Adam Lindemann Sued by Nature Conservancy for Allegedly Installing Julian Schnabel Sculpture Without Permission Fra Angelico's Restored Fiesole Altarpiece Returns to Its Original Church Home After Blockbuster Museum Show.

It has been revealed that as ARTnews reported in April, the dispute centers on Saint Sixtus (ca. 1453–55), a painting by the Italian Renaissance master that Baron Marcel Bich, the founder of Bic, bought at Sotheby’s in 1972 for £130,000. The painting eventually passed to his son Bruno, who kept it in his Fifth Avenue apartment in Manhattan. Then, around 2006, it disappeared.

According to a lawsuit filed in March by Bruno’s three sons, Gonzalve, Charles, and Guillaume, the family’s chauffeur, Roy Morrow, stole the painting and sold it to Feigen for $3 million. The family claims Morrow had no paperwork proving the painting was his, but Feigen bought it anyway and promptly insured it for $8.5 million, nearly three times what he’d paid.

Feigen, one of New York’s best-known Old Master dealers before his death in 2021, later consigned the painting to Christie’s. In 2018, it was sold for $5.4 million to Chilean billionaire Álvaro Saieh and his wife, Ana Guzmán.

In a recent development, the Bich brothers say they didn’t learn where the painting ended up until 2023. They asked for it back the following year, but Saieh and Guzmán refused. So the brothers sued, demanding the painting’s return, along with damages and money from its sale.

Industry observers note that feigen’s representatives tell a different story. In March, lawyers for his estate told Reuters that Morrow had signed a bill of sale saying he owned the painting. The Saiehs, meanwhile, have noted they bought it in good faith, relying on Christie’s research.

Which brings us to the latest ruling.

Feigen’s lawyers argued that the family had simply waited too long to bring its claims. After all, Feigen bought the painting in 2006 and sold it in 2018. The brothers didn’t file their lawsuit until March 2026.

But stolen art can be a tricky business under Latest York law. Generally, when someone buys a stolen artwork in good faith, the clock doesn’t start ticking on a claim for its return until the rightful owner demands it back and the buyer refuses.

Things get more complicated when someone is accused of knowingly dealing in stolen property. The clock can start earlier, and Clynes noted there were too many unanswered questions about Feigen’s purchase to settle the issue now.

According to recent reports, the judge also rejected, for now, an argument that the family had dragged its feet for so long that allowing the case to continue would be unfair. Lawyers call that laches. Both arguments can come up again later.

Sources indicate that feigen’s side did score one win. The judge dismissed claims against his revocable trust and its trustees because the family hadn’t shown enough to connect the trust to the money from the painting’s sale. The brothers can bring those claims again if they find more evidence.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Earlier this month, Trump’s White House ballroom and military bunker laid its final structural steel beam, with politicians and critics weighing in on the scale of the project.

Recently taken images of the extension, which show the structure with massive concrete shear walls, steel beams, and columns, along with a partially enclosed roof structure, have drawn attention to the scale of the building.

No sign of its planned neoclassical ornamentation has yet been implemented.

Officially called the East Wing Modernization Project, the structure dwarfs the Executive Residence and West Wing.

Trump revealed the laying of the last steel beam in the superstructure on 4 November, the day after the national midterm elections.

It has been revealed that “This is a special structure,” Trump said on a tour on 4 November, according to NBC News. “It’s going to be not only one of the biggest, but it’ll be the most beautiful ballroom, I think, anywhere in the world, and they’ve been trying to get it for 150 years.”.

It says everything about Donald Trump that his gilded ballroom dwarfs the size of the People's House—and it says everything about the American people that they repudiated him loudly and clearly last Tuesday. pic.twitter.com/ou23LpAes8.

Since then, there has been a renewed wave of criticism online over the project, ranging from outrage to humour.

Former senator and presidential candidate Hillary Clinton wrote on X (formerly Twitter), commenting on the size of the structure and noting the midterm election’s “repudiation” of Trump.

“It claims everything about Donald Trump that his gilded ballroom dwarfs the size of the People’s House—and it says everything about the American people that they repudiated him loudly and clearly last Tuesday,” wrote Clinton.

Congressman Jim Clyburn took a similar stance in a statement on Facebook, noting that the ballroom was “much bigger” than the rest of the White House.

Industry observers note that architecture critic Kate Wagner took a more humorous approach, noting that the ballroom is not neoclassical in construction. Wagner compared it to a Ramada Inn, a chain of hotels in the US, that they will “glue pediments to”.

It has been revealed that “[It’s] an outcome designed in a lab to make everyone angry. possibly the most trump building ever built,” wrote Wagner on X.com.

The ballroom has been controversial since Trump demolished the White House’s East Wing in October 2025. The National Capital Planning Commission approved the project in April.

It has faced legal challenges, with US District Judge Leon issuing a stay in response to a lawsuit led by the National Trust for Historic Preservation.

the fact that trump's ballroom is clearly not neoclassical in any way shape or form is possibly the funniest moment in architectural history.

In August, the Supreme Court allowed the project to continue, though the dissenting opinion stated it was “likely unlawful”.

Despite the legal challenges, construction has continued, with Trump’s team leaning on the national security aspects of the underground bunker.

Industry observers note that the administration has also floated prepares to add a screening facility at Sherman Park – a small park to the southwest of the White House. Trump also installed a paved helipad on the White House lawn.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the upcoming Grand Theft Auto arrived this week, the messianic reward after 13 long years, offering the best-rendered version of the series’ standing promise: anything, within the scope of its metropolis and the player’s imagination. I watched my cousin paint a house for his avatar’s girlfriend, then hop in a car and drive to the Bass Museum. Or rather, to the Vice City Museum of Art, the faithful replica of it in Vice City, the game’s fictional Miami.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar teased that Grand Theft Auto VI would boast the franchise’s sharpest graphics yet, and the claim was not exaggerated. The Vice Museum of Art captures the Bass’s signature civic Art Deco style: a pale limestone facade (the real stuff was quarried in the Florida Keys) and, as far as I could tell, even the carved decorative relief around the entry. It’s a far cry from the series’ earliest entries, when a building like this would have been a smooth beige box; here, the facade looks textured. We parked and admired its public art: a riff on Miami Mountain, a tower of boulders by Ugo Rondinone permanently installed in Collins Park, outside the Bass. Part of Rondinone’s “Mountain” series, it’s made of garishly clashing fluorescent rocks stacked high and probably visible from space. The Vice City version has swapped stone for emojis: winking, crying, smiling. Related Articles Art Advisor Sophia Cohen on How the Next Generation of Collectors Is Approaching the Art Market Ireland's Experiment in Paying Artists a Basic Income Is Working as Intended For Artists.

It has been revealed that vice City may be hiding another Easter egg for art heads. Months ago, a screenshot circulated online from an expansion for Grand Theft Auto Online, showing a upcoming character in a shirt with an “Art Oregano” logo. It’s a safe bet that it’s a nod to Art Basel Miami Beach, held at the Miami Beach Convention Center, since it’s set in the same font as the fair’s. The herby homage was well received. “I hope he’ll be in GTA 6 having his own little art studio or something,” wrote one Reddit user. Another added, “I can’t wait to wear this shirt to Art Basel this year, if I can pull myself away from GTA6.”.

According to recent reports, art Basel Miami Beach runs December 4-6; keep an eye out for Art Oregano shirts. And, perhaps, as players make it further into the notoriously long game, a newly introduced version of Art Oregano may appear.

Sources indicate that I couldn’t personally verify whether the game includes a replica of the fair, with NPCs entering and exiting, as the Vice Museum did. We’d spent the momentous night mundanely, mostly comparing paint swatches. All of it in line with what viral clips suggest: the game’s characters can do drugs and rob banks—chaos, generally speaking—but we’d rather have time to drive with no destination in mind.

According to recent reports, before I left, my cousin regretfully canceled our plans to visit the Guggenheim on Saturday. He has to work.

Industry News: What's Love Got to Do With It? The Relationship Cycle Explained

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that relationships aren’t just about candlelit dinners and cozy sofa nights — they’re complex AF, filled with ups, downs, twists, and turns.
  • According to recent reports, each relationship phase serves a unique purpose, helping you learn more about each other, yourself, and the kind of relationship you want to build.
  • Whether you’re in the throes of a new romance or navigating the challenges of a long-term commitment, continue reading to learn how to rock each phase like a pro.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that relationships aren’t just about candlelit dinners and cozy sofa nights — they’re complex AF, filled with ups, downs, twists, and turns. From the first flush of love to the settled comfort of commitment, relationships have stages that evolve with time.

According to recent reports, each relationship phase serves a unique purpose, helping you learn more about each other, yourself, and the kind of relationship you want to build. Understanding the dynamics of these stages is crucial for any couple (or throuple!) aiming to develop a lasting bond.

Whether you’re in the throes of a new romance or navigating the challenges of a long-term commitment, continue reading to learn how to rock each phase like a pro.

It has been revealed that from those “can’t eat, can’t sleep” early days to the “let’s build an empire” moments, each relationship stage is like a season of your fave drama binge. But, like any good drama, the plot thickens as time passes and things change. Here’s what to expect, month by month:.

It has been revealed that welcome to the love bubble, where everything about your significant other seems nothing short of magical. The positives overshadow any negatives, creating a blissfully skewed balance sheet of love. It lasts from about 6 months to 2 years for most peeps, but many folks say they are still madly in love even after 20 years together!

Industry observers note that research highlights that during this stage, the prefrontal cortex, which is crucial for critically judging others, shows decreased activity. In other words, you’re less likely to focus on your partner’s faults and more likely to overlook their flaws.

Lurve also activates specific areas in the brain that are driven by goals and rewards. These areas are rich in dopamine and oxytocin receptors, chemicals that make you feel good and bonded to others. They encourage you to pursue and maintain a relationship because it feels rewarding and fulfilling.

It has been revealed that if the euphoric stage is the wild, pulse-racing party of love, the early attachment stage is the cozy after-party where things get real comfortable. In the thrilling initial phase, your brain is doped up on dopamine, but as this initial buzz begins to mellow, a more sophisticated part of the brain starts to step up — the ventral pallidum.

Now, after the first year or so, deeper bonds are formed, helped along by attachment hormones like vasopressin and oxytocin, also fondly known as “the love hormone.” These hormones help transform the electric excitement of upcoming love into a warm, enduring attachment.

According to recent reports, hold tight because the crisis stage hits around 5 to 7 years, and it’s a true test of your relationship’s resilience. This phase often feels like a rollercoaster, where life’s challenges can either pull you apart or push you closer together. Many couples experience a drift during this time, and how you handle it — either by addressing the issues head-on or continuing to drift — can define your future together.

Significant life events, like becoming parents, often occur during this stage and can intensify the pressure. These events can either strengthen your bond through shared responsibilities and mutual love or strain it to the breaking point. Successfully navigating this stage means moving beyond mere survival to fostering a deeper, more meaningful connection.

If you’ve made it this far, congrats, you’re in the deep attachment stage! Post-crisis, you’re looking at 7 years and beyond where you settle into that deep, comfy love. No more daily fireworks — now it’s about a slow-burning ember that warms the house.

In a recent development, you know each other inside and out, warts and all. It’s about unconditional support, knowing looks across crowded rooms, and being each other’s rock. Welcome to the good life!

Recent findings suggest that every relationship is a blend of sweet and sour and everything in between. Understanding the stages, from the initial euphoria to the deep attachment stage, helps you embrace the journey, keep your bond strong, and prepare your heart for whatever comes next. So buckle up and enjoy the ride — it’ll be worth it!

#114466. Breaking: Dezeen Awards 2026 design project of the year winner named

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 12m • 📚 Deep Dive (2482 w)
📖 Baca
General 📈 Bullish 🌐 Dezeen ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Dezeen Awards 2026 design project of the year winner named

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2482 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dezeen

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The wayfinding scheme for London‘s V&A East Storehouse has won Dezeen Awards 2026 design project of the year following the announcement of all 16 design category winners at a party in London.
  • The 16 winners awarded in Dezeen’s annual awards programme include designs by Laurids Gallée and John Tree, as well as Foster + Partners and Kettal.
  • Fieldwork Facility’s graphic identity for the V&A East Storehouse experience won the design project of the year award and was also named graphic design of the year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The wayfinding scheme for London‘s V&A East Storehouse has won Dezeen Awards 2026 design project of the year following the announcement of all 16 design category winners at a party in London.

The 16 winners awarded in Dezeen’s annual awards programme include designs by Laurids Gallée and John Tree, as well as Foster + Partners and Kettal.

Fieldwork Facility’s graphic identity for the V&A East Storehouse experience won the design project of the year award and was also named graphic design of the year.

V&A East Storehouse by Fieldwork Facility.

The master jury cited the project as a “sophisticated wayfinding scheme that demonstrates how signage can do far more than direct: it can define identity, shape experience and establish a sense of place”.

The judges praised the design for its “clarity, confidence and restraint, seamlessly guiding visitors through the V&A East Storehouse while adding to the character of the building”.

V&A East Storehouse was up against designs that included a constellation of gloopy-looking polished resin lights, an electric cargo bike with the carrying capacity of a small van and a low-carbon, concrete-like floor tile strengthened by bacteria.

Read more about all the winning design projects below:.

Design project of the year and graphic design of the year: V&A East Storehouse by Fieldwork Facility.

Design studio Fieldwork Facility was challenged with navigating visitors to the V&A’s storage vault, including 250,000 historic art, craft and design objects – especially a younger, more diverse crowd who might normally feel excluded from museums.

This fun and informative signage and wayfinding perfectly embraces the changing nature of the V&A East Storehouse.

The Hackney design studio looked to an unexpected source of inspiration when creating wayfinding for London’s V&A East Storehouse: Gen-Z apps and services.

“This fun and informative signage and wayfinding perfectly embraces the changing nature of the V&A East Storehouse,” noted the master jury.

“As the displays change, the signage, captions and general wayfinding can be updated efficiently, embracing the adaptability and lack of formality of the museum.”.

Furniture design of the year: Dado Series by Allen Kaufmann Objects.

Berlin studio Allen Kaufmann Architekten won furniture design of the year for its Dado series of tables and shelves.

What is simple in appearance is underscored with a well-resolved and detailed construction made from a monomaterial.

The practice adapted a traditional woodworking joint to create a flat-pack range that can be assembled completely without tools nor glue, screws, brackets or other fasteners.

Sources indicate that “What is simple in appearance is underscored with a well-resolved and detailed construction made from a monomaterial,” the judges said. “The shelving is satisfying to assemble and demonstrates everything furniture needs to be, and no more.”.

The project also won its category for the 2026 public vote.

Seating design of the year: Kino by Pablo Castillo Design.

Barcelona-based designer Pablo Castillo won seating design of the year for Kino, a cantilevered 3D-printed chair for Decibel.

Modern shapes meet zero-waste manufacturing; surely the future.

The designer’s aim was to create a recognisable chair silhouette, while also responding to the specificities of the 3D printing process.

In a recent development, its entire form is printed from PLA, the most common bioplastic, although the material is reinforced with cellulose plant fibres. This increases its strength, enabling the cantilevered seat.

“The 3D printing of furniture is becoming more refined and this is a strong example of that,” mentioned the master jury.

It has been revealed that “The mono-material construction is sophisticated and has a strong aesthetic profile,” they continued. “Modern shapes meet zero-waste manufacturing; surely the future.”.

Collectible design of the year: Lima Charlie by Studio Laurids Gallée.

Austrian designer Laurids Gallée won collectible design of the year for Lima Charlie, a series of five colourful, sculptural lamps.

Mesmerising, intriguing and evocative, these lights are truly original and demonstrate a high level of care in their meticulous craftsmanship.

The lighting collection comprises five hand-cast resin light works and machined aluminium pieces.

In a recent development, first, the designer used digital processes to determine each composition. Then, casting solid blocks of the material before colouring, cutting and sculpting them into shape. Each piece was meticulously sanded and polished to arrive at the desired smooth surface.

“Mesmerising, intriguing and evocative, these lights are truly original and demonstrate a high level of care in their meticulous craftsmanship,” praised the judges. “Beautiful treasures to enhance any space.”.

Bespoke design of the year: Real Time Schiphol People’s Clock by Maarten Baas.

Dutch designer Maarten Baas won bespoke design of the year for The People’s Clock, a choreographed representation of the passage of time at Amsterdam’s Schiphol Airport.

It was an ambitious undertaking to make the piece, which celebrates and gives ownership to the airport workers.

Baas recruited 1,000 participants – the majority being airport employees – to form the hands of The People’s Clock and move in sync, forming the hour and minute hands. The second hand comprises a single person running a lap of the circular perimeter each minute.

“This timepiece in Amsterdam’s busy airport momentarily takes users away from the efficient functionality of the space by providing a reference to the time in a more playful and poetic way,” mentioned the master jury.

“It was an ambitious undertaking to make the piece, which celebrates and gives ownership to the airport workers.”.

Lighting design of the year: Hoop Table Lamp by John Tree for Vaarnii.

Designer John Tree won lighting design of the year for the Hoop Table Lamp for Finnish brand Vaarni.

There is a confidence in the minimal use of materials and a cuteness in the ensuing form.

The monolithic light combines a block of solid pine wood – synonymous with the Finnish brand’s designs – with a hooped shade of thin pine veneer, sourced from a sustainably managed forest.

“We were all drawn to the simple and characterful gestures of this table lamp, which embraces warmth from a common timber,” the judges said.

“There is a confidence in the minimal use of materials and a cuteness in the ensuing form.”.

Architectural lighting design of the year: Cologne Cathedral by Licht Kunst Licht.

Lighting design studio Licht Kunst Licht won architectural lighting design of the year for its illumination of Cologne Cathedral’s historic facade.

This well-considered lighting scheme successfully highlights Cologne’s monumental cathedral as a jewel on the night skyline.

The lighting scheme used more than 700 surface-mounted LED luminaires to transform nighttime views of the world’s tallest cathedral without drilling a single hole in its delicate stonework.

“This well-considered lighting scheme successfully highlights Cologne’s monumental cathedral as a jewel on the night skyline,” the judges praised.

“The light sources are subtly integrated and have managed to reduce energy consumption while creating maximum impact for this city landmark,” they added.

The project also won its category for the 2026 public vote.

Surface design of the year: Basic Third by Pretty Plastic.

Dutch manufacturer Pretty Plastic won surface design of the year for its Basic Third tiles.

There is an inherent beauty and honesty to the product, adding texture and depth to the architecture.

The cladding material was developed by the Pretty Plastic company, started by architecture studios Overtreders W and Bureau SLA.

The tiles, which were made from 30,987 kilograms of post-consumer plastic waste, have been applied as cladding for Plus Ultra III, the first timber laboratory building in the Netherlands.

“Pretty Plastics has chosen to work with the worst kind of plastic – PVC – and found a way to repurpose the material into tiles,” said the judges.

“The material is already fire-compliant and UV stable, making it a worthy contender for the cladding of buildings,” they continued. “There is an inherent beauty and honesty to the product, adding texture and depth to the architecture.”.

Looking ahead, the judges mentioned “its impact will be proven by how easy it is to scale.”.

Textile design of the year: Bianni Wool Paper by Arudeko.

Mexican design studio won textile design of the year for Bianni, a paper-like material made from colourful waste wool.

With so much wool waste in the world, this new material adds value to the waste.

Sourced from the off-cuts of handmade carpets and cushions crafted by local weaving communities in Teotitlán del Valle, Mexico, Arudeko saw the potential to use the surplus material and save it from being discarded.

Bianni can be sculpted into everything from lampshades to room dividers.

“With so much wool waste in the world, this new material adds value to the waste,” the judges commended.

“Furthermore, the processing provides employment to skilled locals, the outcome being an interesting and beautiful paper alternative to be applied to other products,” they said. “There is much potential for further exploration across the world.”.

Workplace design of the year: Area by Foster + Partners and Kettal.

Foster + Partners and Kettal won workplace design of the year for their modular Area table system.

There is an appealing monumentalism to this office desk and a tactility in the simplicity and richness of the material composition.

According to recent reports, designed to be durable and adaptable, Area combines aluminium columns, a panoply of tabletop options and concealed power. The aluminium columns anchor the design, serving as both structural support and discreet container for power cables and electrical components.

“There is an appealing monumentalism to this office desk and a tactility in the simplicity and richness of the material composition,” said the judges.

“There are sophisticated elements and thoughtful hidden details for integrating technology into an otherwise minimalist design,” they continued.

Product design (consumer design) of the year: Pedal 4 by Minimal.

British start-up Minimal won product design (consumer design) of the year for Pedal 4, an electric cargo bike with the carrying capacity of a small van.

A smart fresh vehicle typology that addresses the challenges of inner city deliveries.

The four-wheeled, pedal-assist cargo vehicle was built to take up less room on the roads and evade traffic even on London’s crowded and complex streets. It is now operating in London with delivery companies Royal Mail and Evri.

“A smart new vehicle typology that addresses the challenges of inner city deliveries,” praised the judges.

“This is a great ‘last mile’ replacement for large polluting vans. The slender design manoeuvres easily in city streets while the electric motor emits no noxious pollutants,” they continued.

“The vehicles’ local assembly also allows it to be easily repaired.”.

Product design (health, wellbeing and wearables) of the year: CurifyLabs PharmaPrinter Aurum by Studio Aslak Siimes.

Industrial design firm Studio Aslak Siimes and Finnish startup CurifyLabs won product design (health, wellbeing and wearables) of the year for pharmaceutical compounding system, PharmaPrinter Aurum.

It’s refreshing to see something so functional having also been aesthetically considered.

The system is designed to improve the process of creating patient-specific medicine, born from the realisation that almost 30 per cent of all medication requires personalisation rather than being mass-manufactured, according to studio founder Aslak Siimes.

“This device offers a real innovation in precision healthcare and decentralises the production of pills,” the judges said. “Precise medical doses are prepared bespoke for each customer, reducing waste and eliminating human error.”.

“Furthermore, it’s refreshing to see something so functional having also been aesthetically considered,” they added.

Product design (bathroom) of the year: Dekoda by Kohler Health.

Kohler Health won product design (bathroom) of the year for Dekoda, a health tracker specifically for the toilet.

This is an innovative, early-diagnostic device for ongoing monitoring of health conditions.

Designed to be discreet and intuitive, the tracker clips to the side of the toilet bowl to give insights on gut health and hydration levels, and to detect the presence of blood.

Sources indicate that “This is an innovative, early-diagnostic device for ongoing monitoring of health conditions,” the judges mentioned. “The design of the device is discreet and visually passive, making it suitable for its function in the bathroom.”.

Installation design of the year: Einder for USB002 Tour by Boris Acket and Fred Again.

Visual artist Boris Acket won installation design of the year for Einder, which featured as the standout show design for DJ Fred again..’s USB002 Tour.

This lightweight and flexible installation uses minimum material to maximum effect, making it evocative while sustainable. More please!

The installation features a large suspended sheet of fabric which floats above the audience like a transparent, breathing roof.

Throughout the concert, the sculpture wafts and moves across the audience, creating smaller and larger spaces, static spatial gestures, storms, and water surfaces.

The judges summed up the project as “stunning, emotive, immersive, dynamic, simple”.

Industry observers note that “This lightweight and flexible installation uses minimum material to maximum effect, making it evocative while sustainable. More please!”.

Sustainable design of the year: Datecrete by Datecrete Studio.

Architect Sara Abu Farha and engineer Khaled Shalka won sustainable design of the year for Datecrete, a concrete-style material developed by Abu Farha and Shalka formed from crushed dates.

This is a necessary regional innovation, repurposing an abundant waste material (date pits) into a local construction material, and providing a welcome alternative to concrete.

The project aims to demonstrate how the abundant regional byproduct can become part of an architectural material language. Patent-pending, Datecrete can be produced as floor and wall tiles, cladding, furniture, lighting elements and smaller design objects.

“This is a necessary regional innovation, repurposing an abundant waste material (date pits) into a local construction material, and providing a welcome alternative to concrete,” said the master jury.

“The processing of the pits is decentralised, so it has the potential to scale in communities across the date-growing region.”.

Material innovation of the year: Mimmik Tile by Front.

Dutch sustainability platform Front and biotechnology company Biomason won material innovation of the year for Mimmik, a low-carbon, concrete-like floor tile strengthened by bacteria.

This tile design is genuinely pushing innovation forward in its creation; collaborating with bacteria as a sustainable alternative to concrete.

Front believes Mimmik is the first bacteria-grown tile to be industrially produced, making a sustainable technology available to a wide market of specifiers looking to reduce the carbon footprint of their commercial projects.

“This tile design is genuinely pushing innovation forward in its creation; collaborating with bacteria as a sustainable alternative to concrete,” praised the judges.

Industry observers note that “As such, the embodied carbon is greatly reduced,” they noted. “The production is scalable and could shift the dial in the future production of tiles and paving.”.

In a recent development, dezeen Awards 2026 in partnership with TrimbleDezeen Awards is the ultimate accolade for architects and designers worldwide. The ninth edition of the annual awards is in partnership with global technology organization Trimble. Through connected hardware and software solutions, Trimble helps designers to transform the way they shape spaces and buildings as well as drive productivity in the process. Trimble’s collaboration with Dezeen Awards demonstrates its ongoing commitment to inspiring and supporting creative excellence across the globe.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Over the past couple of years, most of the press releases coming from software companies have contained announcements of new AI features.
  • Canva is one of those companies, and it's introduced a bunch of generative AI tools to its design platform.
  • Canva has added two AI controls for both Free and Pro consumers.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Over the past couple of years, most of the press releases coming from software companies have contained announcements of new AI features. Image, video and vector generation, removal tools, agentic workflows, AI assistants, and myriad other advances that can help artists do in seconds something that used to take hours.

Canva is one of those companies, and it's introduced a bunch of generative AI tools to its design platform. So the email I received yesterday made me do a double take. On the day that Anthropic completed the world's biggest IPO in history, it introduced an 'AI off switch'.

Canva has added two AI controls for both Free and Pro consumers. The generative AI switch can be used to hide all of its generative AI tools, including Magic Write, Magic Design, Magic Expand, Dream Lab and Canva Code. It can be switched on or off at any time.

There's also an option to “See less AI content” on Canva's library of templates and design elements. This addresses complaints about the glut of AI-generated content making it harder to find quality work, something that's been causing problems on platforms as varied as Etsy and ArtStation.

Canva says AI-generated content remains a "small portion" of its library and that such content is identified in its metadata. Turning on the latest function isn't guaranteed to remove it completely, but it should put human-made templates and design elements first in search results and recommendations.

Recent findings suggest that the addition of a couple of toggles to the UI wouldn't normally be breaking news, so the fact that Canva feels this deserved its own announcement is telling. After heavily promoting AI tools, it's now presenting the ability to turn them off as a groundbreaking advance – and it is. This might be the first time that a major AI-forward creative software developer has recognised that a sizable portion of its user base just isn't into it.

"We believe AI has extraordinary potential to help people bring their ideas to life, and we're excited to keep pushing the boundaries of what's possible," Canva claims. "At the same time, like so many of you, we know there's something special about the time, care, and creativity that goes into making something that's truly yours.".

An 'AI off button' is something that some creatives have been calling for. Part of the difficulty in implementing one is that it needs a definition of AI. Programs like Adobe's Photoshop have used machine learning for many years; it just wasn't branded as 'AI'. Many artists welcome tools that speed up their work, but not ones that do the creation part for them, especially if they're powered by models that were trained on unlicensed work.

Canva's recognised that. The toggle only turns off generative AI tools, such as ones that generate new imagery, text or code from prompts. Assistive editing tools like Background Remover or Magic Grab, which lets you select and move an object in an image will still be available. Using them won't cause your work to be shamed with metadata identifying it as AI-generated.

A 'no AI button' also requires a willingness from the provider. Since generative AI features are often charged on a per-use basis via credits, software companies generally want to encourage their customers to use them.

Adobe teased some impressive-looking AI-powered tools in the Adobe Max Sneaks presentation last week, but it's also clear that some customers detest generative AI, which has created a market for fresh tools like the artist-led Niva app, which is promoting itself as AI-free art software.

Will an AI-off button let Canva have its cake and eat it?

El Greco Masterpiece Gets Its Colors Back After More Than 400 Years

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (892 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Artnews

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that king Philip II of Spain wasn’t particularly impressed with El Greco‘s The Martyrdom of Saint Maurice and the Theban Legion when he first saw it.
  • It has been revealed that A painstaking nine-month restoration, recently finished, has found the monumental painting looking considerably more like the one El Greco envisioned.
  • The restoration was conducted at Madrid’s Royal Collections Gallery, under the supervision of Rafael Alonso, an 81-year-old former Prado Museum restorer, who has spent decades working on El Greco’s paintings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that king Philip II of Spain wasn’t particularly impressed with El Greco‘s The Martyrdom of Saint Maurice and the Theban Legion when he first saw it. The following four centuries of dirt, varnish, and enthusiastic repainting hadn’t done the picture any favors, either.

It has been revealed that A painstaking nine-month restoration, recently finished, has found the monumental painting looking considerably more like the one El Greco envisioned. The muddy browns and sickly greens that had dulled the picture for generations are gone. In their place are brilliant blues, reds, yellows, and purples, along with a newfound depth that had been buried beneath grime. Related Articles AI Model Reveals Latest Information About Authorship of 17th-Century El Greco Altarpiece 15th-Century Bellini Altarpiece in Venice to Be Restored While the Public Watches.

The restoration was conducted at Madrid’s Royal Collections Gallery, under the supervision of Rafael Alonso, an 81-year-old former Prado Museum restorer, who has spent decades working on El Greco’s paintings. The project was supported by the Fundacion Callia in partnership with Spain’s Patrimonio Nacional, which oversees the country’s royal collections.

Recent findings suggest that the results were reported in detail by El País, whose writer followed the restoration from the painting’s removal from El Escorial in February through its finished restoration in October. And what a job it was.

According to recent reports, alonso had initially expected the restoration to take about four months. But once he and fellow restorer Adela Murgui began cleaning the enormous canvas, which measures nearly 15 feet high and 10 feet wide, they discovered that its condition was far worse than even feared.

It has been revealed that “When I put the cotton to the painting, my heart sank,” Alonso told El País. Centuries of varnish and repainting had darkened the colors and flattened the composition. In the 19th century, he explained, painters had simply painted over damaged areas, often adding their own interpretations of what El Greco intended.

Industry observers note that the restorers spent months carefully stripping away those additions, revealing the original paint beneath. Afterward, the repaired the damaged areas using soluble materials, taking pains not to add anything that couldn’t be removed later.

The restoration is particularly striking given the painting’s rather unhappy beginnings.

Industry observers note that el Greco painted The Martyrdom between 1580 and 1582 for the basilica at El Escorial, Philip II’s vast monastery and palace outside Madrid. The king wanted a powerful statement of Catholic faith, while the artist hoped the commission might secure him a permanent position as a court painter.

Neither’s wish was totally granted.

It has been revealed that rather than concentrate on the grisly execution of Saint Maurice and his fellow Christian soldiers, El Greco pushed the violence into the background. Up front, he placed a group of handsome soldiers in brightly colored clothing, their elongated bodies and theatrical poses exemplary of the skills he had learned in Venice and Rome.

Sources indicate that philip II apparently admired the painting’s quality, paying the artist a substantial sum of 800 ducats, but felt it wasn’t right for its intended religious setting. The work was relegated to another room, and El Greco never clinched the royal appointment he’d hoped for.

The painting stayed there for most of the next 444 years, apart from a trip to Madrid for an exhibition in 1999, all the while gradually losing most of its remarkable color and atmosphere.

The restoration also marks another achievement for the Fundacion Callia, founded by Carmen Reviriego, which has helped restore works by Zurbarán, Rubens, Brueghel the Elder, Velázquez, and others through its partnership with Madrid’s Royal Academy of Fine Arts of San Fernando. According to El País, the foundation has helped mobilize €5 million for the preservation of artworks.

Industry observers note that when ARTnews spoke with Reviriego in March, she described Callia as an “incubator of patrons,” bringing together collectors and philanthropists from Spain, Latin America, and beyond. Her goal is to encourage a stronger culture of private support for the arts in a country that has traditionally relied heavily on public funding.

Reviriego had specifically mentioned The Martyrdom during that interview as an example of the work the foundation hoped to support. “El Greco was the Jeff Koons or Damien Hirst of his day,” she told ARTnews this week, “and Phillip II was the most power man and greatest patron of the 16th century.”.

Sources indicate that there’s a nice historical symmetry here. Reviriego argued that great works of art are rarely the achievement of an artist alone. Without patrons, many wouldn’t exist at all. She pointed to the Royal Collections themselves, built in part through the patronage of Philip II, the very king who commissioned The Martyrdom more than four centuries ago. Now, private patronage has helped give that painting a new life.

It has been revealed that for Alonso, meanwhile, the completed restoration marks something of a farewell. After decades spent working on El Greco’s paintings, he told El País that The Martyrdom was the last of the artist’s great masterpieces still awaiting restoration.

The newly restored painting is expected to go on temporary display at Madrid’s Royal Collections Gallery before returning to El Escorial. This time, visitors will get a much better idea of what Philip II saw more than four centuries ago.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

What's your FI number? Calculate it in 60 seconds.

The one number that changes everything.

What $10,000 grows to at different rates over 30 years — the rate difference matters more than you think.

$10,000 invested for 30 years at 6% annual return.

$10,000 invested for 30 years at 8% annual return.

$10,000 invested for 30 years at 10% annual return.

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

In a recent development, future value (FV) is the projected worth of an investment at a specific point in the future, based on an assumed rate of growth. It answers the most practical question in investing: "If I invest this money today, what will it be worth in 10, 20, or 30 years?".

It has been revealed that future value calculations rest on compound interest — the principle that your returns earn their own returns over time. Albert Einstein reportedly called compound interest "the eighth wonder of the world," and while the attribution is debatable, the math is not. The difference between simple interest (returns on your original investment only) and compound interest (returns on your investment plus accumulated returns) becomes enormous over long time horizons.

The basic future value formula for a lump sum investment is:.

For example, $10,000 invested at 8% for 20 years:.

FV = $10,000 x (1.08)^20 = $10,000 x 4.661 = $46,610.

The table reveals two critical insights. First, small differences in return rates produce massive differences over long periods — $10,000 at 6% grows to $57,435 over 30 years, while the same amount at 10% grows to $174,494. That 4-percentage-point difference triples the outcome. Second, time is the dominant variable. At 8%, your money doubles roughly every 9 years — so 30 years gives you more than three doublings, turning $10,000 into over $100,000.

According to recent reports, most people do not invest a single lump sum and walk away. They invest regularly — monthly or per paycheck — over decades. The future value of a series of regular contributions uses a different formula called the future value of an annuity:.

FV = PMT x [((1 + r)^n - 1) / r].

Where PMT is the periodic contribution, r is the periodic rate, and n is the total number of periods.

It has been revealed that in practice, you do not need to calculate this by hand. The insight that matters is this: regular contributions are far more powerful than most people realize because each contribution starts its own compounding clock. Your first $500 contribution compounds for the full 30 years, while your 360th contribution (at month 360) compounds for just one month — but together they build wealth that dwarfs a single lump sum.

In a recent development, A person investing $500 per month at 8% for 30 years accumulates $745,180 — from total contributions of only $180,000. That means $565,180, or 76% of the final balance, came from compound returns rather than your own deposits. This is the engine of wealth building.

Every future value calculation should be done twice — once in nominal terms and once in real (inflation-adjusted) terms. The nominal return is the raw number your investments earn. The real return subtracts inflation, showing you what your money will actually buy.

Sources indicate that historically, the S&P 500 has returned roughly 10% nominally and 7% after inflation. The difference matters enormously over long periods:.

According to recent reports, that $1.13 million in nominal terms has the purchasing power of roughly $610,000 in today's dollars — still excellent, but nearly half less than the headline number suggests. When planning for FI, always use real returns (6-7%) rather than nominal returns (9-10%) to avoid overestimating what your portfolio will actually support in retirement spending.

The Rule of 72 is the simplest and most useful mental math tool in investing. Divide 72 by your annual rate of return to estimate how many years it takes for your investment to double:.

This works in reverse too. If you want to know what rate of return you need to double your money in 15 years: 72 / 15 = 4.8%. The Rule of 72 is an approximation — it is most accurate for rates between 5% and 12% — but it is remarkably precise within that range and far faster than pulling out a calculator.

According to recent reports, the FI community uses future value calculations as the backbone of retirement planning. The process works in three steps:.

The table highlights how starting balance and monthly contribution interact. Notice that increasing your monthly contribution from $1,500 to $2,500 (a $1,000 increase) with a $100,000 starting balance cuts 3.5 years off your time to $1 million. This is the savings rate lever in action — the amount you save each month matters more than any other variable you control.

According to recent reports, A common question is whether it is better to invest a lump sum now or spread contributions over time (dollar-cost averaging). The math is clear: lump sum investing wins approximately two-thirds of the time because markets trend upward over the long term. However, dollar-cost averaging reduces the psychological risk of investing a large amount right before a downturn and provides a behavioral advantage that keeps many investors on track. For most FI-seekers, the question is academic — you invest each paycheck as it arrives because you do not have a large lump sum sitting on the sidelines.

Free calculators, a personalized FI roadmap, and a community of 25K+ on the same journey.

Sources indicate that when projecting your portfolio growth for retirement planning, use real (inflation-adjusted) returns of 6-7% rather than nominal returns of 9-10%. A $1 million nominal balance in 30 years has the purchasing power of roughly $550,000 in today's dollars at 2% average inflation. Planning with real returns ensures you are targeting a portfolio that can actually support your desired spending level.

According to recent reports, track your actual spending for 3 months and annualize it. Multiply by 25 to get your FI number using the 4% safe withdrawal rate. If you spend $60,000 per year, your FI number is $1,500,000.

According to recent reports, add up all retirement accounts (401k, IRA, Roth IRA, HSA), taxable brokerage accounts, and savings. Exclude home equity and non-liquid assets. This is your starting balance for the future value calculation.

Subtract your monthly spending from your monthly after-tax income. Include employer 401(k) match and any other automatic savings. This is your periodic contribution amount for the future value formula.

Use the future value of a lump sum plus annuity formula, or a simple online calculator, to project when your current balance plus monthly contributions will reach your FI number. Use 7% real return (after inflation) for conservative planning.

Sources indicate that test what happens if you increase contributions by $200/month, $500/month, or $1,000/month. Seeing the concrete impact of a savings rate increase — often shaving 2-5 years off your FI timeline — makes the trade-offs tangible and motivating.

Sources indicate that for long-term stock market projections, use 7% for inflation-adjusted (real) returns or 10% for nominal returns based on the S&P 500 historical average. For a more conservative estimate, use 6% real. For bond-heavy portfolios, use 3-4% real. Always specify whether you are using nominal or real returns — mixing them up is one of the most common planning mistakes.

Future value calculations show what WOULD happen if returns were constant every year. In reality, markets fluctuate — you might earn 25% one year and lose 15% the next. Over 20-30 year periods, average returns tend to converge toward historical norms, making future value projections reasonably useful for planning. Treat them as directional estimates, not guarantees.

Future value asks: "What will $10,000 today be worth in 20 years?" Present value asks the reverse: "What is $50,000 in 20 years worth in today's dollars?" They use the same variables but in opposite directions. Present value is useful for evaluating whether a future payout (like a pension or annuity) is worth the cost today.

It has been revealed that the Rule of 72 works for any compounding rate, including inflation. At 3% inflation, prices double every 24 years (72 / 3 = 24). This means $50,000 in annual spending today becomes $100,000 in 24 years in nominal terms — your purchasing power is halved if your income stays flat. This is why investing in assets that outpace inflation is essential.

Recent findings suggest that for FI planning, future value is more intuitive — it tells you what your portfolio will grow to. However, the most practical approach is to calculate future value using real (after-inflation) returns. This effectively gives you a future value stated in today's purchasing power, which is what you actually need to know for spending planning.

According to recent reports, in tax-advantaged accounts (401k, IRA, Roth IRA, HSA), your investments compound without tax drag, so the standard future value formula works directly. In taxable accounts, capital gains taxes, dividend taxes, and tax-loss harvesting all affect your real return. A rough adjustment is to reduce your assumed return by 0.5-1.0% for taxable accounts to account for ongoing tax drag.

Sources indicate that future value calculations are the most practical tool in the FI planner's toolkit. They turn abstract concepts like compound growth and savings rate into concrete dollar amounts and specific timelines. The key takeaways are straightforward: use 7% real returns for conservative planning, always account for inflation by using real rather than nominal returns, and remember that your monthly contribution rate has a far larger impact on the outcome than chasing an extra point or two of return. The Rule of 72 gives you instant mental math for any investment decision — how long to double, what rate you need, and how inflation erodes purchasing power. Combined with a clear FI number and a disciplined savings rate, future value projections show you exactly when financial independence becomes reality. Run the numbers, test different scenarios, and let the math motivate you to increase that monthly contribution whenever you can.
